answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day contract expiration create urgency, but the 94% assembly line utilization removes margin for error. Memory_c4 demonstrates that renegotiation recovered real margin at renewal—directly applicable to the current cost mandate. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing without narrowing scope, which could satisfy the 18% target while preserving stability. Memory_c2 warns against sole-sourcing with the low-cost vendor due to SLA misses on a critical line—this blocks a simple switch. Memory_c1 shows incumbent renewal maintains integration stability. I am verifying memory_c2 to confirm the criticality/SLA risk profile of the primary line, and memory_c6 to validate whether a longer-term commitment structure can achieve the cost target without destabilizing delivery. The recommended action is aggressive renegotiation with the incumbent, leveraging market benchmarking (proven in c4) while exploring extended terms for volume pricing (c6 pathway). This preserves the stable incumbent relationship (c1), avoids sole-source risk (c2 constraint), and defers the add-second-source option (c3) to the next cycle if renegotiation fails. The decision trades short-term contractual flexibility for cost recovery and delivery certainty under high utilization.
